uncited: Multi-View and Parallax-Based Rendering generates volumetric or holographic imagery by computing multiple distinct perspective views of a scene and displaying them on hardware that separates these views spatially or angularly to create a 3D effect.

The family shares the core mechanism of decomposing a 3D representation into a set of 2D views, each corresponding to a specific camera position or holographic aperture, and mapping these views to a display medium that enforces spatial or angular separation.
**View Generation**: A set of $N$ views is generated.
**Display Mapping**: The views are mapped to a display device.
A pre-processing framework for rendering Computer-Generated Holograms (CGH) on autostereoscopic light-field displays.
It consists of four sequential steps applied to the hologram to acquire reconstruction images corresponding to views from a camera rotating around the scene.
**View extraction**: A window with the resolution of the vertical axis of the hologram moves along the horizontal axis to acquire sub-holograms that simulate a pinhole camera view.
The concept of multi-view rendering for volumetric displays has evolved alongside autostereoscopic and light-field display technologies.
